originalConceptPrompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one polished hero illustration for AuthCrunch, a Caddy authentication portal and authorization system. Wide 16:9 landscape, high resolution, exceptionally finished campaign artwork.
Required theme: unmistakably BOTH authentication portal AND authorization. Show a recognizable elegant sign-in portal with username and masked password fields, then identity/role information being evaluated by a distinct access-policy stage, then a protected application. Authentication proves identity; authorization grants or denies application access. Visually distinguish these two stages. A padlock alone, generic abstract glass shapes, or architecture without a portal is insufficient.
Art direction: comparable to the finest RapidKnot technology hero images: physically convincing optical glass, tactile materials, exact edges, restrained atmospheric depth, beautiful editorial lighting, sophisticated composition. AuthCrunch cobalt blue #245bca and navy #172b4d, natural whites or deep navy as specified; subtle green for allowed access and restrained warm coral for denied access.
Framing: show the complete main composition with breathing room; readable visual hierarchy at website size; no cropped-off subject. This is a finished IMAGE of the concept, not a full website mockup. The sign-in UI is part of the artwork, not an entire screenshot.
Text: only a very small number of clean, correctly spelled interface labels specified below. Render portal fields and short labels with precise modern sans-serif typography. No paragraphs, no fake code, no random characters, no valid credentials or tokens, no watermark, no invented brand logo, no giant marketing headline.
Avoid: stock cybersecurity photo, hoodie hacker, binary rain, neon cyberpunk, cluttered dashboards, arbitrary bridges or buildings, floating meaningless icons, toy-like plastic, excessive bloom.
Scene: an elevated three-quarter view of an exquisite architecture-like tabletop technology model with no literal buildings. A prominent upright white-and-cobalt authentication portal panel at left displays username and masked password fields and a blue "Sign in" button. A single delicate cobalt channel carries a small glass identity token from that portal to a distinct central navy authorization hub, which has a crisp small label "Access policy" and three finely machined output channels. Two channels pass through tiny green permission indicators to two elegant frosted-glass application windows, while the third stops at a closed coral-accented permission gate BEFORE a third subtly dimmed application window. The three windows are clean recognizable app surfaces, not dashboards full of data. The image communicates one identity, different application access rules. Pale cool-white background, premium ceramic and anodized metal plus crystal glass, soft museum-quality daylight, precise contacts and restrained glass refraction, crisp near-subject focus, ordered flowing wide composition. Only visible words: "Sign in", "Access policy".
selectedEditPrompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Input image: the supplied image is the edit target, the user-approved AuthCrunch concept number 04. Create ONE refined variation by replacing ONLY the central authorization device.
Preserve: the entire wide 16:9 composition, the exact elevated three-quarter camera, pale cool-white studio, floor reflections and directional daylight, the large glass sign-in portal on the left with its original fields and "Sign in" button, the identity token on its incoming cobalt conduit, all THREE application windows at the right (folder, chat, and dimmed gear), their current positions and scale, and the two green allow indicators and one red deny indicator. Keep the inlet and three outlet connection points consistent with the original scene. Do not crop, rearrange, remove, or add applications.
Requested improvement: replace the squat generic navy router/puck in the middle with the particular elegant authorization device specified below. The new middle object must feel like a beautiful and purposeful access-policy mechanism, not a domestic networking router or a generic network switch. Keep it in the same central footprint, with one identity-bearing input from the left and three policy-controlled outputs at the right.
Material and image quality: agency-level photorealistic product CGI, exceptionally well-designed silhouette, precise optical glass, satin cobalt blue #245bca, deep navy #172b4d, restrained brushed aluminum, physically plausible refraction, clean contacts, subtle tactile detail. Match the existing lighting and visual sophistication of the image. Improve form and craftsmanship, not merely color.
Text: preserve "Sign in". The central device may carry exactly one small, beautifully typeset "Access policy" label. No other new text, invented branding, watermark, or code.
Do not change anything outside the central device except the immediate contact shadows, reflections, and short pipe join sections needed to integrate the replacement. Return the full composition as one finished landscape image, not a crop, contact sheet, or design board.
Central device variation A — GLASS GATEWAY:
Replace the squat hub with a single upright, sculptural optical-glass gateway. A slim navy U-shaped frame holds a thick clear, softly beveled glass policy pane; a small elegant shield-with-check emblem is etched into its center. A precise cobalt identity conduit enters its left edge, and three clean output collars emerge from its right edge, still aligned with the existing app paths. The transparent glass should reveal a simple inner permission aperture rather than fake circuitry. Thin brushed-metal trim, clean open negative space, superb architectural proportions, a low understated support foot. Put the small "Access policy" label near the foot of the pane. It must feel refined, light, and unmistakably an access-control gateway. No giant padlock, no tall black monolith, no chunky router enclosure.
